questions.q: What are the six sections of the enterprise data governance strategy document, in order?
options: Introduction, Budget, Org Chart, Timeline, Appendix, Signatures
Executive Summary, Current State, Target State, Roadmap, Governance Model, Success Metrics
Current State, Executive Summary, Success Metrics, Target State, Roadmap, Governance Model
Only two sections: Problem and Solution
questions.explain: The lesson lays out this exact six-section order as the document skeleton every strategy document in this career path follows.

questions.q: What is the key difference between Lesson 15's deliverables package and Lesson 16's strategy document?
options: There is no difference; they are the same file renamed
The strategy document replaces and deletes the package
The package is for executives and the document is for stewards only
The package is fourteen reference files readable in any order; the document is one synthesized narrative meant to be read start to finish
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly distinguishes the package (reference material, any order) from the document (one narrative, sequential read).

questions.q: Why is the Executive Summary written last even though it appears first in the document?
options: Because it summarizes the whole document, which can't be condensed accurately until everything else is written
Because it is the least important section
Because of alphabetical ordering rules
It is actually written first, not last, according to the lesson
questions.explain: The lesson states the Executive Summary is written last but placed first, since it has to summarize content that doesn't yet exist until the rest is drafted.

questions.q: How does this lesson frame the roadmap's four phases (Foundation, Control, Operationalize, Extend)?
options: As a single phase that hasn't started yet
As purely hypothetical future work with no connection to prior lessons
As phases that contradict the operating model from Lesson 12
As phases already completed across Lessons 2-14, presented as a progress report rather than a proposal
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly maps each roadmap phase to already-completed lessons and frames this as a progress report, which is itself part of the pitch to executives.

questions.q: What closes out the Success Metrics section, tying the document back to its Executive Summary?
options: A list of unrelated software licensing costs
A disclaimer that no metrics are currently tracked
The same six-week DSAR from the Executive Summary now carries a ten-business-day response target, measured monthly
A request to delete the golden Customer record
questions.explain: The lesson closes Success Metrics by circling back to the DSAR incident from the Executive Summary, now expressed as a measured KPI target from Lesson 11.
